subject: biology
intro: Biology leads to the study and stewardship of living systems — molecular research, disease investigation, wildlife science and the lab work that underpins modern medicine.

roles.title: Biochemists and Biophysicists
roles.what: Study the chemical composition and physical principles of living cells — the complex reactions of metabolism, growth and heredity — and test how foods, drugs, hormones and other substances affect tissues.
roles.where: Biological molecules (unit 4), enzymes (unit 5) and respiration (unit 12) teach the reaction chemistry of cells; chromosomes, genes and proteins (unit 17) ground the molecular genetics side.

roles.title: Microbiologists
roles.what: Investigate the growth, structure and development of microscopic organisms — bacteria, algae, fungi — including medical microbiology: how microbes cause disease and how antibiotics act on them.
roles.where: Diseases and immunity (unit 10), cell structure (unit 2) and the drugs topics (unit 15) cover pathogen biology and antibiotic action; biotechnology (unit 21) extends microbes into tools and products.

roles.title: Zoologists and Wildlife Biologists
roles.what: Study the origins, behaviour, diseases, genetics and life processes of animals and wildlife, collecting and analysing biological data to judge how present and potential land and water use affects habitats.
roles.where: Classification (unit 1), variation and selection (unit 18) and the ecosystems units (19 and 20) — energy flow, food webs, conservation — are the field-biology core of this career.

roles.title: Epidemiologists
roles.what: Investigate the determinants and distribution of disease, disability and health outcomes in populations, and develop the means for their prevention and control.
roles.where: Diseases and immunity (unit 10), sexually transmitted infections (16.6) and human influences on ecosystems (unit 20) train the transmission-and-population thinking disease detectives use.

roles.title: Biological Technicians
roles.what: Assist biological and medical scientists: set up and maintain laboratory instruments, monitor experiments, collect samples and data, and analyse organic substances such as blood, food and drugs.
roles.where: The practical micro-sequence — cell structure and specimen sizing (unit 2), diffusion and osmosis investigations (unit 3), enzyme rate experiments (unit 5) — is bench-work training.

roles.title: Genetic Counselors
roles.what: Assess individual and family risk for inherited conditions, explain the genetics and testing options involved, and support families in making informed decisions and coping with what they learn.
roles.where: Inheritance (unit 17) — chromosomes, mitosis, meiosis and monohybrid crosses — plus reproduction (unit 16) give the pedigree-and-probability reasoning counselors translate for patients.
